summary.name: MiniSim
summary.one_liner: A lightweight, open source, native menubar app for launching iOS and Android emulators without opening Android Studio or Xcode.
use_cases: Launching iOS or Android emulators from the menu bar
Avoiding opening Android Studio or Xcode just to start a simulator
Copying device names or IDs for custom CLI commands
Toggling TalkBack accessibility on Android emulators
Restarting a misbehaving emulator with a cold boot
Controlling emulators from the keyboard via Raycast
summary.what_it_does: MiniSim sits in the macOS menu bar and lists your iOS and Android emulators so you can launch them directly. It can copy a device's name and ID for use in CLI commands, and toggle TalkBack accessibility on Android emulators. It can launch an emulator without audio and paste clipboard contents into an emulator. A cold boot option restarts an emulator, and a Raycast extension lets you control it from the keyboard.
notable: Open source and fully native, sits in the menu bar
Launches iOS and Android emulators without Android Studio or Xcode
Toggle TalkBack and paste clipboard to emulator
caveats: Page does not state pricing or license details
Page says more features are coming soon, so the feature set may change
